title: candidate-feedback-draft-julia-park-2026-04-18
content:
Candidate: Julia Park
Role: Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Interviewer: Michael Chen (+ Priya Desai co-review)
Interview date: 2026-04-18
Stage: Onsite loop (design + coding + system Q)

Quick summary:
- Strong systems-first engineer, good intuition for throughput/latency tradeoffs.
- Solid C++/Python background, has production experience optimizing inference pipelines at scale.
- Implementation in the coding task was pragmatic but a bit verbose; got to a correct design and iterative improvements.
- System design discussion showed good awareness of batching, KV-cache, and model-variant routing.

Technical notes (rough):
- Coding exercise: implement a simplified batching queue for token requests with latency SLO; Julia produced a working single-threaded version quickly, then extended to a lock-free-ish ring-buffer idea. Correctness: good. Edge cases: initial version didn't consider backpressure signal to clients; after prompt she added a simple backpressure/count-based shedding strategy.
- Complexity: O(1) enqueue/dequeue in her final proposal; memory bounded by max-batch * concurrent-workers.
- Languages: prefers C++ for perf-critical paths, comfortable prototyping in Python. Mentioned using folly/absl in past teams.
- System design: proposed an architecture with router -> per-model shard queues -> batching workers -> GPU workers. Batching strategy: dynamic batch sizing with max latency budget and sequence-length-aware estimation.
  - Pros: realistic, aligns with how we think about auto-batching.
  - Cons: only briefly mentioned KV cache invalidation semantics (would have liked more on cache consistency when model variants change).
- Observability: emphasized per-request tracing and token-level cost accounting; suggested sampling 1% of requests for full trace.

Behavioral / culture fit:
- Team player, asked good follow-ups about how teams roll out model updates.
- Past experience includes owner of a small infra service (3 people) — seems comfortable shipping and operating.
- Communication: clear, but can be slightly terse when under time pressure.

Strengths:
- Deep operational experience with inference workloads and latency-cost tradeoffs.
- Practical engineer who balances correctness and shipping.
- Familiarity with our core problem space (batching, routing, autoscaling).

Concerns / areas to probe further:
- Networking and multi-tenant isolation at deeper level (e.g., side-channel concerns, GPU memory isolation). She has high-level ideas but limited hands-on with hardware-level isolation and kernel tuning.
- Quantization/low-level kernel optimization experience is moderate — may need ramp-up for low-level runtime kernel work.
- Cross-team influence: solid IC but unclear history of driving large cross-org initiatives.

Scorecard (0-5) - my gut:
- Technical (systems + coding): 4
- Design (architecture + tradeoffs): 4
- Ownership & execution: 4
- Culture fit / communication: 3.5
- Overall recommended: Strong hire for infra/serving team; "hire" for IC role but consider pairing with senior runtime engineer if primary focus is kernel-level perf.

Suggested next steps:
- Loop debrief: Priya to lead calibration with Claude (runtime) and SRE hiring panel.
- If we move forward, consider tasking Julia with a 2-week pairing project to assess kernel tuning aptitude (small spike on quantized GEMM or batching microbenchmark).

Open questions to ask next time (if onsites continue):
- Concrete example of a perf regression she diagnosed end-to-end (symptom -> root cause -> fix -> validation).
- Any direct exposure to CUDA kernel debugging or profiling (nsight, nvprof) beyond perf counters?
- Experience with model-variant fallbacks and canary rollouts where stateful caches exist (how to maintain cache correctness during canary).

Notes to self (for calibration):
- Strong fit for "serving runtime implementation" work (batching, routing, observability).
- Might not be immediate plug-and-play for deep kernel work; budget for training/mentorship.
- Culture: likely to be a strong individual contributor; ambiguous on scaling to manager/owner of cross-team initiatives.

Draft conclusion blurb for hiring doc: "Julia Park is a highly capable systems engineer with solid production experience in inference and strong practical judgment around batching and routing. I recommend hiring for the Serving Runtime team as an IC with mentorship on low-level kernel optimization; recommend extending an offer contingent on standard references and a short technical pairing task."

-- Michael
(Notes are draft; will refine after Priya/Jordan calibration)
